chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Fuzayl ibn Usman, from Abu Ubayda, who said:
I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'When two believers meet and shake hands, Allah turns His Face towards them both, and the sins fall away from their faces until they separate.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for shaking hands between two believers according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), emphasizing the handshake (al-tasaful) as a tangible means of spiritual purification where divine favor is manifested and sins are shed like dust. This practice underscores the Shia emphasis on physical gestures of brotherhood as conduits for grace, linking social interaction directly to metaphysical cleansing.
